statedReasoning: Per the důvodová zpráva (Obecná část) of the government bill signed by Minister of the Environment Petr Hladík (electronic signature 08.12.2025, Ministerstvo životního prostředí), the amendment's primary and explicitly stated purpose is ADAPTATION of Czech law č. 542/2020 Sb. (o výrobcích s ukončenou životností) to directly-applicable EU Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries and waste batteries, which repealed Directive 2006/66/ES and took effect 18 August 2025. Because the battery rules moved from a directive to a directly-applicable regulation, provisions of 542/2020 whose content now flows directly from the regulation are deleted, and enforceability/applicability provisions are inserted. Beyond mandatory adaptation the bill states three secondary aims: (1) combating free-riding across all extended-producer-responsibility (EPR) products via a higher kauce for individually-compliant producers and mandatory collective compliance for certain products; (2) resolving a historical burden of industrial batteries (~211,000 solar installations, ~2 GWh / ~20,000 t by end-2024, take-back cost ~1.4 bn CZK, many producers untraceable) through a collective-compliance financing scheme; and (3) implementing Ekoaudit proposals and fixing legislative-technical defects, this being the first major amendment since the law took effect 1 Jan 2021. It also amends conformity-assessment law č. 90/2016 Sb. (new §27h, Czech-language requirement) and market-surveillance law č. 87/2023 Sb. The stated RIA claims a budget-neutral effect, only slight added administrative burden, and positive environmental and employment effects.
researchedContext: Independent research confirms the bill is a faithful, largely non-discretionary transposition/adaptation exercise. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 entered into force 17 Aug 2023 and became fully applicable 18 Aug 2025, replacing Directive 2006/66/EC, binding manufacturers, importers, distributors and recyclers directly with phased obligations: more ambitious collection targets, stricter recycling efficiency and material-recovery rates, mandatory recycled-content minimums, carbon-footprint declarations, a digital battery passport, and supply-chain due diligence, backed by heavy fines. The most consequential real-world effect flagged by independent commentators concerns EPR economics: the regulation shifts full financial responsibility for collecting, treating and recycling batteries onto producers and constrains contractual cost-shifting; cost-recovery pricing is 'difficult to implement in a price sensitive market.' The Czech bill layers on national mechanisms (higher kauce, mandatory collective compliance, historical-burden financing) that go modestly beyond bare transposition. Per the Poslanecká sněmovna record the bill was submitted by the Government on 10 Dec 2025, had its first reading on 1 July 2026, and is in Environmental Committee review.

unstatedEffects.effect: EPR compliance costs will in practice be absorbed into producer margins or passed into product prices; because the regulation's free-of-charge take-back obligation limits itemised cost pass-through and this is 'difficult to implement in a price sensitive market,' the burden falls hardest on smaller importers/producers and may modestly raise prices — an effect the DZ downplays as 'negligible.'
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Large compliant producers and established recyclers/collective systems that can absorb fixed compliance and reporting costs; disadvantages small importers and marginally end consumers.

unstatedEffects.effect: The bill's higher kauce for individually-compliant producers, mandatory collective compliance for certain products, and use of collective systems to finance the untraceable ~1.4 bn CZK solar-storage historical burden entrench incumbent collective-compliance operators and raise entry barriers — a distributional/competition downside the DZ frames only positively as 'narovnání podmínek na trhu.'
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Incumbent collective compliance systems and their existing large producer members, who gain scale and reduced free-rider leakage while new/small entrants face higher deposits and forced collective membership.

conflictAssessment: Weak-to-negligible; best characterised as a structural governance question, not a genuine self-dealing conflict. The bill is a mandatory adaptation to a directly-applicable EU regulation (2023/1542), scheduled by the Government's 2024 Legislative Work Plan, which Hladík signs ex officio as Minister of the Environment — his discretion over whether and broadly how to transpose is minimal. Of his graph-linked companies, only SAKO Brno (Brno's municipal waste-management company) is sector-adjacent to this law, yet (a) it shows 0 CZK of flagged public-contract flow, and (b) the law's mechanism regulates private producers and collective compliance systems via EPR, not municipal downstream waste operators via contracts — so there is no plausible channel from this bill to SAKO's revenues. The headline money figure in his profile (~5.39 bn CZK) is entirely the ARENA BRNO stadium project, unrelated to waste. His remaining ties are 0 or negligible and unrelated. All ties are municipal board/role positions in publicly-owned companies. Net: no evidence of personal or municipal enrichment engineered through this bill; the honest finding is the absence of a conflict, not a scandal.

citations.claim: Tisk 58 is a government bill amending zákon č. 542/2020 Sb. to adapt Czech law to Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries; it also amends 90/2016 Sb. (§27h) and 87/2023 Sb.; signed by Minister Petr Hladík 08.12.2025; free-riding measures, higher kauce, mandatory collective compliance, and ~1.4 bn CZK solar-storage historical burden are stated in the důvodová zpráva.
The amended statute is zákon č. 542/2020 Sb., o výrobcích s ukončenou životností (a real, in-force Czech law).
The bill also amends the conformity-assessment statute (adds §27h on batteries, Czech-language requirement).
The bill also amends the market-surveillance statute, replacing the reference to Directive 2006/66/ES with Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.
Bill document index (Tisk 58/0): 'Návrh zákona včetně důvodové zprávy' and related PDFs, distributed 10 Dec 2025.
Sponsor is the Government (represented by Ministry of Environment); submitted 10 Dec 2025; first reading 1 July 2026; guarantor Environmental Committee.

Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 shifts full financial responsibility for collecting/treating/recycling batteries onto producers and constrains passing costs to end-users under the free-of-charge take-back obligation — cost-recovery pricing is 'difficult to implement in a price sensitive market.'
SAKO Brno, a.s. is Brno's municipal waste-management company (sector-adjacent to the law) but shows 0 CZK of flagged public-contract flow, and is not the regulated party under this EPR bill.
The dominant money figure among Hladík's linked companies (~5.39 bn CZK) is the ARENA BRNO stadium project, unrelated to waste/end-of-life products.
